cards.title: Reception / Your Desk
cards.description: A cramped desk near the entrance. A whiteboard task board is already overflowing with sticky notes from three different handwriting styles. Post-its on every surface. Your laptop isn't even set up yet.
cards.image_prompt: A cluttered startup reception desk with an overflowing whiteboard task board covered in colorful sticky notes in three different handwriting styles. Post-its on the ceiling, a laptop still in its box, coffee cups everywhere. Warm orange lighting, comedic chaos, flat illustration style.

cards.title: Marco's Kitchen Lab
cards.description: A test kitchen that doubles as an office. Grease-stained recipe binders lean against a monitor showing food photos. The sauce wall has 47 labeled bottles. Somewhere under the chili flakes is a cost spreadsheet.
cards.image_prompt: A chaotic startup test kitchen with grease-stained recipe binders, a wall of 47 labeled sauce bottles, food photos on a monitor, chili flakes scattered over papers. A cost spreadsheet buried under ingredients. Warm oranges and reds, comedic clutter, flat illustration.

cards.title: Diana's Corner Office
cards.description: Dual monitors, both showing spreadsheets. Whiteboards covered in numbers with red circles around alarming ones. A countdown timer on her desk shows minutes until the investor call. Stacks of printed reports marked 'DRAFT — DO NOT SHARE.'
cards.image_prompt: A startup CFO's corner office with dual monitors showing spreadsheets, whiteboards covered in numbers circled in red, a countdown timer on the desk, stacks of draft reports. Clean but stressed. Cool blues and whites with red warning accents, flat illustration.

discoveries.label: Look at the investor questions list

cards.title: Raj's Server Closet
cards.description: A standing desk crammed between two server racks. Monitors show dashboards in various states of green and red. Sticky notes with passwords everywhere. A coffee-stained manual is taped to the wall with several sections unreadable.
cards.image_prompt: A cramped server closet with a standing desk between two blinking server racks. Monitors showing green and red dashboards. Password sticky notes everywhere. A coffee-stained manual taped to the wall with redacted sections. Greens and reds from LEDs, dim lighting, flat illustration.

cards.title: Break Room
cards.description: A kitchenette with a bulletin board overflowing with notes, business cards, clipped articles, and a passive-aggressive sign about labeling your food. The fridge has menus from competitors magneted to it. Someone wrote 'KNOW THY ENEMY' on a sticky note above them.
cards.image_prompt: A startup break room kitchenette with an overflowing bulletin board, competitor menus on the fridge, a passive-aggressive food labeling sign, scattered business cards. A sticky note reading 'KNOW THY ENEMY' above the competitor menus. Warm fluorescent lighting, comedic office culture, flat illustration.

discoveries.label: Look at competitor menus on the fridge
Compile the research briefing for Diana

cards.title: Chocolot
cards.description: A sleek, dimly-lit chocolate dessert bar. Mood lighting. Leather booths. The menu is on a backlit board — their 'AI-Powered Flavor Matching' is suspiciously similar to QuickBite's recommendation engine. A barista polishes glasses while watching the room. Security cameras blink red.
cards.image_prompt: A sleek dimly-lit chocolate dessert bar with mood lighting, leather booths, and a backlit menu board. A suspicious barista polishes glasses while watching. Security cameras blink red. Dark chocolate browns with neon accents, spy-comedy noir atmosphere, flat illustration.

cards.title: Panini Gemelli
cards.description: A bright Italian fast-casual spot. Checkered tablecloths. A chalkboard menu with hand-drawn pasta illustrations. Two identical men in matching aprons work the floor — one waves warmly, the other scans the room with narrow eyes. A 'NOW HIRING — 2ND LOCATION' sign just got flipped face-down.
cards.image_prompt: A bright Italian fast-casual restaurant with checkered tablecloths and a chalkboard menu. Two identical twin owners in matching aprons — one waving warmly, one suspicious. A hiring sign being flipped face-down. Warm Italian reds and greens, spy-comedy atmosphere, flat illustration.

cards.title: Tabouleh Express
cards.description: The loading dock behind a Mediterranean restaurant, 6 AM. Fluorescent dock lights buzz. Delivery vans idle. Stacks of ingredient crates labeled in three languages. People mill about — drivers checking phones, kitchen staff grabbing coffee, a woman with a binder near the office door. Seven people mill around the loading dock — drivers, cooks, suppliers. Some look like they know things. Others are clearly just clocking out.
cards.image_prompt: A busy delivery dock behind a Mediterranean restaurant at dawn. Fluorescent lights buzzing, delivery vans idling, stacks of crates in three languages. Various workers milling about — a driver with a clipboard, a cook on break, an assistant with a binder. Dawn blues and oranges, spy-comedy noir, flat illustration.

cards.title: The Cooker
cards.description: A trendy gastropub with exposed brick and Edison bulbs. Above the bar: a massive screen cycling through customer posts, reviews, and blog mentions — 'The Cooker Social Wall.' In a corner booth, a young woman frantically types on a laptop, occasionally groaning and hitting delete. Posts on the wall are disappearing mid-sentence.
cards.image_prompt: A trendy gastropub with exposed brick and Edison bulbs. A massive screen above the bar shows social media posts that are flickering and disappearing. A stressed young woman in a corner booth frantically types on a laptop. Dark moody lighting with screen glow, spy-comedy noir, flat illustration.

discoveries.label: Talk to the Social Media Manager
Read the reviews before they vanish

cards.title: War Room
cards.description: A glass-walled conference room. The speakerphone is already ringing. Diana stands at the head of the table, slides loaded on the big screen. Three investor faces appear — polite smiles that could turn skeptical any second. Marco hovers in the doorway with a Volcano Burger sample 'just in case.'
cards.image_prompt: A glass-walled corporate conference room with a speakerphone ringing. A woman stands at the head with slides on a big screen. Three investor faces on a video call with polite smiles. A chef hovers in the doorway holding a burger. Clean professional space, tension and pressure, flat illustration.

cards.title: Store #10
cards.description:
An empty restaurant. Bare concrete floors with tape marking where booths will go. Wires hang from the ceiling. A stack of flat-pack tables sits in the corner. The walk-in fridge hums but the door is propped open. Everything COULD be ready by tomorrow — if someone figures out what's missing and automates the rest.

A laminated poster on the wall shows the 8-step opening sequence from Store #9: 1. Confirm health inspection 2. Set up WiFi and tablets 3. Test POS system 4. Calculate food cost 5. Marco approves menu 6. Print menus 7. Order opening-day inventory 8. Send social media announcement. Someone scribbled underneath: 'This time, Quick automates ALL of it.'
cards.image_prompt: An unfinished restaurant with bare concrete floors marked with tape, wires hanging from the ceiling, flat-pack furniture stacked in corners. A humming walk-in fridge with its door propped open. The skeleton of a restaurant waiting to be born. Construction yellows and concrete grays, hopeful potential, flat illustration.

discoveries.label: Watch Quick execute the full chain

cards.title: Whiteboard Task Board
cards.description:
A chaotic whiteboard with tasks in three handwriting styles. Marco's (large, exclamation marks): 'VOLCANO BURGER LAUNCH!!!' Diana's (precise, red ink): 'Investor deck — 55 min.' Raj's (cramped, apologetic): 'Fix POS sync, sorry.'

Pinned in the corner: a faded sticky note from the previous assistant who quit. It reads:

"Day 1 survival guide: (1) Find where everything IS before doing anything. (2) Organize the mess so you can actually find things later. (3) Get connected to the vendor systems. (4) THEN go gather intel on competitors. (5) Only build the investor deck once you have real data. (6) Automation is always the last step — you can't automate chaos.

Good luck. I lasted 3 weeks. — Alex"
cards.image_prompt: A chaotic whiteboard covered in sticky notes and three different handwriting styles — one large and excited, one precise in red ink, one cramped and apologetic. No clear organization. Startup chaos aesthetic, warm palette, flat illustration.

cards.title: Recipe Data Fragments
cards.description: Grease-stained recipe cards, Marco's secret notebook, supplier invoices, and a POS export buried under chili flakes. Raw ingredients for calculating the true food cost.
cards.image_prompt: A collection of grease-stained recipe cards, a small notebook, supplier invoices, and a computer printout. All slightly messy and food-stained. Warm kitchen tones, startup chaos, flat illustration.

cards.title: POS Export Terminal
cards.description: A greasy monitor showing the SquareBite POS dashboard. Sales data, transaction logs, and unit costs — all exportable. The keyboard has hot sauce on the space bar.
cards.image_prompt: A greasy computer monitor showing a POS dashboard with sales data and charts. The keyboard has a hot sauce stain on the space bar. Kitchen setting, tech meets food chaos, flat illustration.

cards.title: Food Cost Analysis
cards.description: The complete food cost breakdown for QuickBite's menu. Volcano Burger: 32% food cost ratio at scale. Marco's wagyu habit exposed — but the numbers work.
cards.image_prompt: A clean analysis document showing food cost breakdowns with charts and percentages. A burger illustration with cost arrows. Professional but with a coffee ring stain. Warm tones, data visualization, flat illustration.

cards.title: Data Sources Whiteboard
cards.description: Diana's whiteboard listing five data sources: POS Revenue, Staff Hours, Supplier Invoices, Customer Ratings, Delivery Times. Arrows point to question marks. She needs them CONNECTED to investor questions.
cards.image_prompt: A whiteboard with five data source labels connected by arrows to question marks. Clean handwriting in red and blue markers. Financial office setting, organized but incomplete, flat illustration.

cards.title: Investor Questions List
cards.description: Diana's prep sheet: 'What's our profit margin?' 'Are we overstaffed?' 'Who's our cheapest supplier?' 'Are customers happy?' 'Is delivery too slow?' Plus two decoys Diana crossed out: 'Marco's favorite color?' and 'When's Raj's birthday?'
cards.image_prompt: A printed list of investor questions with checkboxes. Five serious business questions and two silly ones crossed out in red. Professional but humorous. Clean paper with red pen marks, flat illustration.

cards.title: Financial Data Card
cards.description: Data sources linked to the right questions. POS answers profit margin. Staff Hours answers overstaffing. Supplier Invoices reveals cheapest supplier. Diana nods: 'Finally. Someone who gets it.'
cards.image_prompt: A structured document with data sources connected by colored lines to business questions. Clean and organized, with a small 'approved' stamp. Blue and green tones, professional data visualization, flat illustration.

cards.title: Coffee-Stained Manual
cards.description: The Quick Automate connection manual. Most of it is readable, but key sections are obscured by coffee damage. Visible rules hint at the correct activation sequence. 'Payment Gateway must be activated before [STAIN] Portal.'
cards.image_prompt: A technical manual taped to a wall with large coffee stains obscuring portions of text. Visible text shows connection rules. Server closet setting, dim lighting, flat illustration.

cards.title: Automation Panel
cards.description: Five colored wires labeled: POS System (red), Supplier Portal (blue), Staff Scheduler (yellow), Delivery Tracker (green), Payment Gateway (white). They need to be activated in the correct sequence.
cards.image_prompt: A panel with five colored wires — red, blue, yellow, green, white — each labeled with a system name. Numbered positions 1-5. Server closet setting with blinking LEDs, flat illustration.

cards.title: Systems Data Card
cards.description: Automation panel connected in correct sequence: Payment, POS, Scheduler, Supplier, Delivery. All systems online. Raj is tearing up. 'It works. It actually works.'
cards.image_prompt: A systems dashboard showing five connected services all glowing green with checkmarks. A small tear-drop emoji in the corner. Dark background with green status lights, flat illustration.

cards.title: Bulletin Board Fragments
cards.description: Scraps of paper, Post-its, and torn printouts from all three founders. Quotes about food costs, system crashes, customer complaints, and kitchen operations — all jumbled together. Needs organizing into categories.
cards.image_prompt: A cluttered bulletin board with scraps of paper, Post-its, and torn printouts in various handwriting styles. Pins, tape, and coffee rings. Break room setting, organized chaos, flat illustration.

cards.title: Competitor Menus
cards.description: Four competitor menus stuck to the fridge: Chocolot (desserts, premium pricing), Panini Gemelli (Italian, simple menu), Tabouleh Express (delivery-only Mediterranean), The Cooker (gastropub, expensive). Someone circled their prices in red.
cards.image_prompt: Four restaurant menus stuck to a fridge with magnets. Each has different styling and price points circled in red marker. A sticky note above says 'KNOW THY ENEMY.' Break room setting, flat illustration.

cards.title: Research Briefing
cards.description: All data organized into Quick Spaces: Kitchen Ops, Finance, Systems, Customer Intel. The combined view reveals four competitor locations worth investigating. Diana: 'Now go get me citations.'
cards.image_prompt: A professional briefing document with four color-coded sections and a map showing four competitor locations marked with pins. Clean layout with the QuickBite logo. Professional tones, organized from chaos, flat illustration.

cards.title: Combined Data (Partial)
cards.description: Recipe data and financial data merged — food costs meet revenue metrics. Still missing systems data from Raj to complete the picture.
cards.image_prompt: Two overlapping documents merging together with a progress bar showing 2/3 complete. Warm and cool tones blending, flat illustration.

cards.title: Suspicious Barista
cards.description: The Chocolot barista — polishes glasses while watching the room. Notices everything.

cards.title: Chocolot Menu Board
cards.description: Backlit menu: 'AI-Powered Flavor Matching' (suspicious). Dark Truffle Mocha $9.50. Ganache Croissant Melt $14.20 (anchor item). Co-Pilot Truffle: 'Our algorithm chose this flavor for you.' Premium pricing across the board.
cards.image_prompt: A sleek backlit menu board with premium chocolate dessert items and suspicious AI-themed names. Dark chocolate aesthetic with neon accents, spy-comedy noir, flat illustration.

cards.title: Pricing Intel (Chocolot)
cards.description: Complete pricing structure photographed: anchor item margins, loyalty tiers, seasonal promo calendar. Their AI branding is marketing fluff — same desserts, fancier names. Cost structure higher than QuickBite per unit.
cards.image_prompt: A collection of covertly taken phone photos showing menu prices, a loyalty card, and a promotional calendar. Spy-camera aesthetic with slightly tilted angles. Dark mood, flat illustration.

cards.title: Gemelli Twin (Friendly)
cards.description: The friendly Gemelli twin — waves at every customer, talks too much about business plans.

cards.title: Gemelli Twin (Suspicious)
cards.description: The suspicious Gemelli twin — watches you with narrow eyes, catches inconsistencies.

cards.title: Chalkboard Specials
cards.description: Hand-drawn pasta illustrations and daily specials. Three paninis, two soups, one salad — that's the whole menu. A 'NOW HIRING' sign was recently flipped face-down. Simple operations, clearly scalable.
cards.image_prompt: A charming Italian chalkboard menu with hand-drawn pasta illustrations. Simple menu with only six items. A hiring sign visible face-down nearby. Warm Italian restaurant tones, flat illustration.

cards.title: Expansion Intel (Gemelli)
cards.description: Confirmed: location #4 on Fifth Street signed, targeting 5 by October. Everything runs from one iPad. Simple menu = easy replication. Biggest competitive threat for expansion speed.
cards.image_prompt: A dossier page with expansion timeline, a map with four location pins, and a quote about 'simple menu, easy replication.' Spy-dossier aesthetic with stamped classifications, flat illustration.

cards.title: Tony the Driver
cards.description: Tony — gossipy delivery driver. Loves to chat while loading crates. Knows every restaurant's business.

cards.title: Delivery Schedule Board

cards.image_prompt: A delivery dock whiteboard with route maps, time slots, and a new corporate catering column highlighted. A 12-block radius map with a circled delivery guarantee. Dawn lighting, industrial setting, flat illustration.

cards.title: Social Media Manager
cards.description: The Cooker's social media manager — stressed, deleting bad reviews in real-time, accidentally reveals staffing problems.

cards.title: The Social Wall

cards.image_prompt: A massive screen above a bar showing social media posts that are flickering and being deleted. Some posts are highlighted in red before vanishing. A stressed figure types frantically below. Moody pub lighting with screen glow, flat illustration.

cards.title: Weakness Intel (Cooker)
cards.description: Critical finding: The Cooker's head chef is interviewing elsewhere. Staff overwhelmed, quality dropping, health complaints rising. Their only edge (desserts) won't survive without leadership. Biggest vulnerability in the competitive landscape.
cards.image_prompt: An intelligence report with highlighted weakness findings — a chef silhouette walking away, declining quality graphs, and health warning flags. Dark moody tones with red warning highlights, flat illustration.

cards.title: Research Complete
cards.description: All four competitor intel reports compiled. Diana's calling — the War Room is ready.

cards.title: Pitch Deck
cards.description: Diana's investor slides loaded on the big screen. Seventeen cells filled with your research data. Food cost: 32%. Biggest threat: Panini Gemelli. Satisfaction: 4.6/5. The numbers are all here — now defend them.
cards.image_prompt: A presentation slide on a large conference room screen showing graphs, charts, and key metrics filled in. Clean professional design with QuickBite branding. Conference room setting, flat illustration.

cards.title: Chef Marco (Reception)
cards.description: Chef Marco — bursts through the kitchen door in a hot-sauce-stained apron, demanding food cost data.

cards.title: Diana (Reception)
cards.description: Diana — appears from her office with a phone in each hand, needs competitive analysis with citations.

cards.title: Raj (Reception)
cards.description: Raj — pokes head out of server closet, apologizes for the chaos, mentions everything is on fire.

cards.title: Chef Marco
cards.description: Chef Marco — creative genius, terrible with numbers. Passionate about the Volcano Burger.

cards.title: Diana
cards.description: Diana — data-obsessed CFO. Needs everything with citations. The investor call countdown is ticking.

cards.title: Raj
cards.description: Raj — anxious CIO who built everything in his garage. Systems held together with duct tape.

cards.title: The Searchable Pantry (Quick Index)
cards.description: "You know how I can never find my own recipes? Diana wanted the food cost but the recipe was in my binder, the portions were in my notebook, and the prices were in her spreadsheet. Quick Index is like having one giant searchable pantry — you tell it where all your ingredients live, and it finds them when you need them. No more digging through drawers." — Marco

cards.title: Numbers Into Answers (Quick Sight)
cards.description: "Numbers without context are noise. Quick Sight takes your raw data — sales, costs, ratings — and turns them into answers. Not just charts. Answers. I ask 'which store has the best margin?' and it tells me. In English. With a chart I can show investors who think Excel is cutting-edge technology." — Diana

cards.title: The System That Orders Buns (Quick Automate)
cards.description: "Every one of these systems — POS, suppliers, scheduling, delivery — used to be a phone call. Or a ticket. Or a sticky note that fell behind the rack. Quick Automate connects them so actions happen automatically. Not 'I'll get to it Thursday' automatically. Actually automatically. The system that orders buns when stock hits 20%? That's Automate." — Raj

cards.title: Label Your Lunch (Spaces)
cards.description: "This bulletin board? It's the analogue version of Spaces. Kitchen stuff, money stuff, tech stuff, customer stuff — all jumbled together. Quick Spaces lets you create dedicated areas: Kitchen Ops space, Finance space, Systems space. Everyone puts their stuff in the right place, and anyone can find it. Revolutionary? No. But neither is labeling your lunch, and nobody does that either." — Raj

cards.title: Citations, Citations, Citations (Quick Research)
cards.description: "What you just did in there — observing, gathering data points, noting patterns — that's Quick Research. Except Quick Research does it with documents, databases, and public sources instead of a phone camera. It synthesizes everything into a report with citations. Diana's favorite word: citations." — Narrator

cards.title: Selling The Future (Quick Sight Scenarios)
cards.description: "What-if analysis. That's the part that wins the money. Not 'here's what happened' — investors know the past. 'Here's what happens IF we open 6 stores, IF chicken prices rise 15%, IF the Volcano Burger does what we think.' Quick Sight Scenarios let you adjust the variables and show them the future. A future where they make money." — Diana

cards.title: The Checklist That Runs Itself (Quick Flows)
cards.description: "Every store opening used to be a scramble. Store #6 opened without a freezer. Store #8 forgot napkins for a WEEK. Quick Flows is the checklist that runs itself. Step 1 triggers step 2. Step 2 won't run until step 1 actually completes. Conditions, dependencies, automatic triggers. You design it once — every future store opens the same way. No scramble. No forgotten napkins." — Raj
